## My Thinking

I've farmed this land my whole life. My mother grew wheat and corn, my neighbors grow wheat and corn, and I grow wheat and corn. There's no reason to change. The land here in Quzhou is good flat land on the plain — it suits wheat and maize. I don't have the schooling to understand new fancy methods, and I'm not going to risk my family's food and income experimenting.

I have about 8 mu of land. I'll plant winter wheat in the autumn after the summer maize comes off, same as always. That rotation is just what you do here.

For seeds, I go to Lao Wang's agricultural supply shop in the village. He always has the good wheat seed — last year everyone was buying Jimai 22, so I'll get that again. For maize, hybrid seed, same brand as last year, it performed well.

Fertilizer — I put down a good amount before planting wheat, mix it in with the rotary tiller. I know some people say you can use less, but I've seen what happens when the wheat looks yellow in spring. I'd rather put a bit more and sleep at night. Same for corn.

Irrigation is critical here. Not enough rain. For wheat I'll water three times at least — once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. For maize, maybe twice if summer is dry like last year.

I'll spray herbicide early for both crops. For wheat I'll do a second spray if I see rust or aphids.

For corn, I just plant directly into the stubble after the wheat harvest — no time for tillage, and the moisture stays in better anyway.
